topics.title: A 20-year-old female university student presents on 2026-09-28 with 4 days of fever (38.7 C in clinic), severe sore throat, headache and marked fatigue that began on 2026-09-25. Exam shows exudative tonsillitis, tender posterior cervical lymphadenopathy and a spleen tip palpable 2 cm below the costal margin. Labs on 2026-09-28: WBC 13.8 x10^3/uL with 62% lymphocytes (18% reactive/atypical), absolute neutrophil count 3,100/uL, hemoglobin 13.2 g/dL, platelets 148,000/uL, ALT 96 U/L, AST 74 U/L, creatinine 0.72 mg/dL (weight 58 kg); urine hCG negative. Monospot is positive and EBV serology shows VCA IgM positive, VCA IgG positive and EBNA IgG negative; HIV antigen/antibody and CMV IgM are negative. She has never had a mononucleosis-like illness before, has no chronic medical conditions or autoimmune disease, and has received no corticosteroids. Current medications are acetaminophen and ibuprofen as needed plus a combined oral contraceptive pill; she is not breastfeeding.
topics.hidden_details: 20-year-old female university student. Symptom onset 2026-09-25 (fever, sore throat, headache, fatigue); seen 2026-09-28 (illness day 4). Temperature 38.7 C. Exudative tonsillitis, tender posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, spleen tip palpable 2 cm below costal margin; no airway compromise. Labs 2026-09-28: WBC 13.8 x10^3/uL, lymphocytes 62% with 18% reactive/atypical lymphocytes, ANC 3,100/uL, Hb 13.2 g/dL, platelets 148,000/uL, ALT 96 U/L (ULN 35), AST 74 U/L, creatinine 0.72 mg/dL; weight 58 kg, estimated Cockcroft-Gault CrCl approx. 114 mL/min. Urine hCG negative. Monospot positive; EBV serology VCA IgM positive, VCA IgG positive, EBNA IgG negative (primary EBV infection, confirmed by the treating clinician). HIV Ag/Ab negative, CMV IgM negative; no other intercurrent viral infection. No previous mononucleosis-like illness. No primary or secondary immunodeficiency, no immunosuppressive or immunomodulating medication, no corticosteroids ever for this illness. No history of autoimmune disease (no SLE, vasculitis, thyroiditis, etc.). Medications: acetaminophen and ibuprofen as needed, combined oral contraceptive pill; no probenecid, trimethoprim, myelosuppressive or nephrotoxic drugs. Not pregnant, not breastfeeding; willing to add condoms for double-barrier contraception through 90 days after any study treatment. No other chronic conditions. Currently febrile and acutely ill (not in good general health). Willing to provide informed consent, to donate blood and oral wash samples, and able to comply with study visits.
topics.design_note: Acute primary EBV infection on day 4 with all hematologic/renal thresholds met, so eligible for both the SLE-autoantibody cohort (NCT05127980) and the valomaciclovir trial (NCT00575185, <=7 days, VCA IgM+/EBNA IgG-). Current febrile illness and elevated ALT make her clearly ineligible for the healthy-volunteer EBV vaccine trial.

topics.title: A 26-year-old man presents on 2026-09-28 with 5 days of fever, sore throat and malaise that started on 2026-09-24; temperature today is 38.9 C. Exam shows enlarged tonsils with exudate, bilateral posterior cervical lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly on ultrasound (15 cm). His past history is notable for autoimmune (Hashimoto) thyroiditis with positive anti-TPO antibodies diagnosed in 2023, well controlled on levothyroxine 75 mcg daily (TSH 2.1 mIU/L in 2026-06); he has never had a mononucleosis-like illness and has never taken corticosteroids or other immunosuppressants. Labs on 2026-09-28: WBC 11.2 x10^3/uL with 58% lymphocytes including many reactive lymphocytes, ANC 2,400/uL, hemoglobin 14.6 g/dL, platelets 162,000/uL, ALT 142 U/L, creatinine 0.95 mg/dL (weight 78 kg). Monospot is positive and EBV serology shows VCA IgM positive with VCA IgG and EBNA IgG both negative; HIV antigen/antibody and CMV IgM are negative. Apart from levothyroxine he takes only acetaminophen.

No immunodeficiency; never received corticosteroids, cytotoxic drugs, interferons or other immunosuppressive/immunomodulating drugs. No prior mononucleosis-like illness. Labs 2026-09-28: WBC 11.2 x10^3/uL, lymphocytes 58% with many reactive lymphocytes, ANC 2,400/uL, Hb 14.6 g/dL, platelets 162,000/uL, ALT 142 U/L (ULN 45), creatinine 0.95 mg/dL; weight 78 kg, Cockcroft-Gault CrCl approx. 130 mL/min. Monospot positive; EBV serology VCA IgM positive, VCA IgG negative, EBNA IgG negative (primary EBV infection confirmed by treating clinician). HIV Ag/Ab negative, CMV IgM negative; no other intercurrent viral infection. Medications: levothyroxine and acetaminophen only; no probenecid, trimethoprim, myelosuppressive or nephrotoxic drugs. Female partner of childbearing potential; he is willing to use condoms during and for 90 days after treatment. Currently febrile and acutely ill. Willing to consent, provide blood and oral wash samples, and comply with study visits.
topics.design_note: Decisive violation is a history of autoimmune disease (Hashimoto thyroiditis), which excludes him from NCT05127980, while he meets every criterion of the valomaciclovir trial (day 5, VCA IgM+/EBNA IgG-, labs above thresholds, no steroids). Active febrile illness and ALT >1.25x ULN exclude him from the healthy-volunteer vaccine trial.

topics.title: A 31-year-old woman presents on 2026-09-28 with sore throat, fever to 38.4 C, headache and profound fatigue that began on 2026-09-19. Exam shows pharyngeal erythema with tonsillar exudate, prominent posterior cervical lymphadenopathy and a palpable spleen tip. Labs on 2026-09-28: WBC 12.6 x10^3/uL with absolute lymphocytosis (7.9 x10^3/uL) and 22% reactive lymphocytes on manual differential, hemoglobin 12.8 g/dL, platelets 171,000/uL, ALT 118 U/L, AST 90 U/L. A monospot test is positive and EBV VCA IgM is positive; the remainder of the EBV antibody panel was still pending at the time of this note. Her treating clinician considers this infectious mononucleosis.
topics.hidden_details: 31-year-old woman. Symptom onset 2026-09-19; seen 2026-09-28 (illness day 10). Temperature 38.4 C. Tonsillar exudate, posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, palpable spleen tip. Labs 2026-09-28: WBC 12.6 x10^3/uL, absolute lymphocytes 7.9 x10^3/uL, 22% reactive lymphocytes, ANC 3,300/uL, Hb 12.8 g/dL, platelets 171,000/uL, ALT 118 U/L, AST 90 U/L, creatinine 0.68 mg/dL (weight 62 kg). Monospot positive. Full EBV panel resulted 2026-09-29: VCA IgM positive, VCA IgG positive, EBNA IgG negative, confirming primary EBV infection (confirmed by the treating clinician). HIV Ag/Ab negative, CMV IgM negative. Past medical history: none; no autoimmune disease (no SLE, vasculitis, thyroiditis, IBD, etc.), no primary or secondary immunodeficiency. Medications: acetaminophen only; no corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive medication, no prednisone at any dose. No prior mononucleosis-like illness. Urine hCG negative, uses a levonorgestrel IUD, not breastfeeding. Willing to consent, provide blood samples, and comply with study visits.
topics.design_note: Full record is eligible for the IM group of NCT05127980, but the title omits the EBNA/VCA IgG results needed to confirm primary-infection serology and her autoimmune/immunosuppression history. Illness day 10 (visible) excludes the valomaciclovir trial (>7 days) and age 31 excludes the 18-29 vaccine trial.

topics.title: A 68-year-old man presents on 2026-09-28 with flashes and floaters in the right eye beginning on 2026-09-25, followed on 2026-09-26 by a painless curtain spreading from below and loss of central vision. He had uncomplicated right cataract surgery with a posterior-chamber IOL in 2025-03 and has never had retinal surgery. Dilated exam of the right eye shows a macula-off rhegmatogenous retinal detachment involving the superotemporal, inferotemporal and inferonasal quadrants, caused by a horseshoe tear at 10 o'clock and a second horseshoe tear at 7 o'clock; there is no vitreous hemorrhage, no proliferative vitreoretinopathy and no other retinal disease, and right visual acuity is counting fingers. The left eye is phakic with visual acuity 20/25 and a normal fundus. He is scheduled for right pars plana vitrectomy with SF6 gas tamponade on 2026-09-30. His history is otherwise limited to hypertension and hyperlipidemia treated with amlodipine and atorvastatin, with no gastrointestinal, hepatobiliary, gallbladder or pancreatic disease and no known drug or food intolerances.
topics.hidden_details: 68-year-old man. Right eye: flashes/floaters from 2026-09-25, curtain and central vision loss from 2026-09-26 (macula off for 2-3 days at 2026-09-28 visit). Pseudophakic right eye (uncomplicated phacoemulsification with PCIOL 2025-03); no prior vitrectomy or retinal surgery. Macula-off RRD involving superotemporal, inferotemporal and inferonasal quadrants (3 quadrants). Two horseshoe tears: 10 o'clock and 7 o'clock (inferior half; tears span >2 clock hours). No vitreous hemorrhage, no PVR, clear media, no other retinal pathology (no AMD, diabetic retinopathy, or vascular occlusion). Right VA counting fingers, IOP 12 mmHg. Left eye phakic, VA 20/25, normal fundus; not monophthalmic. Scheduled for right PPV with SF6 gas tamponade on 2026-09-30. Medical history: hypertension (well controlled), hyperlipidemia; medications amlodipine 5 mg, atorvastatin 20 mg. No peptic ulcer, no acute/chronic liver disease, no gallstones or biliary disease, no pancreatic disease, no Crohn's disease/ulcerative colitis or other intestinal disease, no galactose intolerance/lactase deficiency/glucose-galactose malabsorption, no known hypersensitivity to bile acids or other drugs. No cholestyramine, colestipol, Al/Mg antacids, smectite, cyclosporine, ciprofloxacin, nitrendipine or dapsone. Not in any other interventional study; not under protective custody; has health insurance. Willing to consent and able to comply with study visits.
topics.design_note: Designed as a clear candidate for the UDCA trial (pseudophakic, 3-quadrant macula-off RRD <=7 days, scheduled PPV, no hepatobiliary/GI exclusions). The inferior 7 o'clock tear (and tears spanning >2 clock hours) excludes both the superior-tear pneumatic retinopexy trial and the iSeelr trial.

topics.title: A 58-year-old postmenopausal woman with high myopia (about -5.0 D spherical equivalent in both eyes) presents on 2026-09-28 with 2 days of flashes, new floaters and a shadow in the inferior visual field of the left eye. Left visual acuity is 6/9 and both lenses are clear (phakic). Dilated fundus exam of the left eye shows a macula-on rhegmatogenous retinal detachment in the superonasal quadrant from a single horseshoe tear at 1 o'clock, with no vitreous hemorrhage, no signs of proliferative vitreoretinopathy and a clear view of the retina. The right eye has visual acuity 6/6 and no retinal breaks. Pneumatic retinopexy with SF6 gas and laser photocoagulation is planned for the next day, and she confirms that she can maintain the required head positioning at home. She has well-controlled hypertension on lisinopril and no other ocular history.
topics.hidden_details: 58-year-old postmenopausal woman (menopause at 52). High myopia approx. -5.0 D spherical equivalent both eyes (axial lengths 26.4 mm right, 26.6 mm left). Left eye: 2 days of flashes/floaters and inferior field shadow; VA 6/9; phakic with clear lens; macula-on RRD confined to the superonasal quadrant from a single horseshoe tear at 1 o'clock (upper half, within 1 clock hour); no additional breaks, no inferior tears, no vitreous hemorrhage, no PVR, clear media; IOP 14 mmHg. Right eye: VA 6/6, no breaks. No prior vitrectomy or ocular surgery, no ocular trauma, no glaucoma. Planned management: pneumatic retinopexy with SF6 and laser on 2026-09-29; no vitrectomy scheduled. Able and willing to maintain postoperative head positioning (lives with spouse who will assist). Medical: hypertension controlled on lisinopril; no liver, GI, or biliary disease. Willing to consent and able to comply with study visits.
topics.design_note: Classic pneumatic retinopexy candidate (single superior tear, no PVR/VH, can position), eligible for NCT06694259. Phakic, macula-on status with no vitrectomy planned excludes the UDCA trial, and macula-on detachment plus myopia >-4 D excludes the iSeelr trial.

topics.title: A 74-year-old woman presents on 2026-09-29 with flashes of light and floaters in the right eye that began on 2026-09-26, followed on 2026-09-27 by a dark curtain descending from above and blurred central vision. She had bilateral cataract surgery with posterior-chamber IOLs in 2025 (right eye 2025-02, left eye 2025-05). Examination of the right eye shows a bullous macula-off rhegmatogenous retinal detachment involving the superotemporal and superonasal quadrants, caused by two horseshoe tears at 10:30 and 1:30 o'clock; there is no vitreous hemorrhage and no clinical sign of proliferative vitreoretinopathy, and right visual acuity is hand motions. Left visual acuity is 6/7.5. She has hypertension controlled on losartan (BP 132/78 mmHg) and takes an aluminum/magnesium hydroxide antacid daily for reflux symptoms. She is being evaluated for surgical repair.
topics.hidden_details: 74-year-old woman. Right eye: flashes/floaters from 2026-09-26, curtain and central blur from 2026-09-27 (macula off approx. 2 days; recent onset). Bilateral pseudophakia (PCIOL right 2025-02, left 2025-05); pre-cataract refraction -1.25 D spherical equivalent both eyes; axial lengths 23.9 mm right and 23.8 mm left. Right eye: bullous macula-off RRD, superotemporal and superonasal quadrants; two horseshoe tears at 10:30 and 1:30 o'clock (both superior; together spanning 3 clock hours); no inferior tears, no vitreous hemorrhage, no PVR signs (no flare, vitreous clumps, pigment clusters, rolled edges or star folds); VA hand motions; IOP 15 mmHg. Left (fellow) eye: VA 6/7.5, IOP 14 mmHg, normal macula, 360-degree peripheral exam without lattice degeneration or breaks, no sight-threatening pathology or structural abnormality, no planned surgery. No history of glaucoma or IOP >21 mmHg in either eye, no ocular trauma, no prior intraocular infection, no current ocular or systemic infection. No family history of retinal detachment; no Marfan or Stickler syndrome or other collagen disorder. Medical: hypertension controlled on losartan (BP 132/78); no diabetes; GERD treated with daily oral aluminum/magnesium hydroxide antacid; no liver disease. Low anaesthetic risk (ASA II) and able to lie supine for more than 1 hour. Lives 15 minutes from the hospital with family support; can attend all study visits and the emergency department if needed. Not pregnant or breastfeeding. Willing to consent and able to comply with study visits.
topics.design_note: Full record meets every iSeelr criterion (age >=50, recent macula-off RRD from superior tears only, fellow eye 6/7.5, no myopia >-4 D, glaucoma, lattice, family history or PVR), but the title omits the refractive/axial-length history, glaucoma/IOP history and fellow-eye periphery and family history. Visible daily Al/Mg antacid excludes the UDCA trial and two superior tears spanning 3 clock hours exclude the pneumatic retinopexy trial.
